BRINDLEWOOD PHARMACEUTICAL GROUP
Clinical Development Update: BRW-7724 (azoleptamine hydrochloride)
Internal Briefing Document — Q4 2023

Program Background

BRW-7724, known by the proposed international nonproprietary name azoleptamine, is a selective dopamine D3 receptor partial agonist under development at Brindlewood Pharmaceutical Group's neuroscience division in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The compound was first synthesized by the medicinal chemistry team led by Dr. Fatima Osei-Bonsu in March 2018. Preclinical studies demonstrated nanomolar binding affinity (Ki = 0.34 nM at D3; >1,000-fold selectivity over D2) and favorable CNS penetration in rodent models (brain-to-plasma ratio of 3.7 at steady state).

Phase IIb Results Summary

The Phase IIb dose-ranging study (Protocol BRW-7724-201) enrolled 312 adult patients aged 22–64 diagnosed with moderate-to-severe major depressive disorder (MDD) at 24 investigational sites across the United States and Canada between January 2021 and November 2022. Patients were randomized 1:1:1 to azoleptamine 20 mg once daily, azoleptamine 40 mg once daily, or matched placebo for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score at week 8.

At the 20 mg dose, mean MADRS reduction was 2.4 points (SD 6.1) versus 1.9 points (SD 5.8) for placebo (p=0.41; not significant). At the 40 mg dose, mean MADRS reduction was 3.1 points (SD 5.7) versus 1.9 points for placebo (difference = 1.2 points; 95% CI: 0.3–2.1; p=0.009). Response rate (defined as ≥50% MADRS reduction) was 58.7% for the 40 mg group versus 29.8% for placebo (odds ratio 3.28; 95% CI: 1.84–5.84; p<0.001). Remission (MADRS ≤10) was achieved by 33.4% of azoleptamine 40 mg patients and 17.1% of placebo patients at week 8.

Safety and Tolerability

The most common treatment-emergent adverse event at the 40 mg dose was dizziness, occurring in 24.0% of azoleptamine patients versus 8.3% of placebo patients. Nausea was reported by 18.7% of the 40 mg group. Three serious adverse events were reported in the azoleptamine arms, none of which were adjudicated as drug-related by the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board. No clinically significant QTc prolongation was observed. Discontinuation due to adverse events occurred in 9.4% of the 40 mg group versus 4.8% of placebo.

Drug Interaction Profile

In vitro studies indicate azoleptamine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and a mild inhibitor of CYP2D6 (IC50 = 4.7 µM). A dedicated drug-drug interaction study (BRW-7724-106) conducted with the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor itraconazole demonstrated a 3.1-fold increase in azoleptamine area under the curve, establishing the need for dose adjustment in patients receiving strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. No significant interaction was observed with the CYP2D6 substrate dextromethorphan at the planned therapeutic dose.

Phase III Design

Brindlewood plans to initiate the Phase III program (Protocol BRW-7724-301) in Q2 2024 with enrollment of 680 patients at 30 investigational sites across eight countries. The study will evaluate azoleptamine 40 mg versus placebo over a 12-week double-blind period followed by a 40-week open-label extension. Co-primary endpoints are MADRS change at week 8 and Sheehan Disability Scale total score at week 12. Enrollment is expected to complete in approximately 18 months. Total estimated Phase III program budget is $138 million, inclusive of regulatory filing costs estimated at $11.4 million.

Regulatory Strategy

Brindlewood submitted a Type C meeting request to the FDA's Division of Psychiatry on September 18, 2023, requesting alignment on the Phase III primary endpoint and patient population. The agency's response, received November 2, 2023, confirmed acceptability of the MADRS primary endpoint and indicated that a treatment-resistant MDD (TRMDD) population (defined as failure of ≥2 prior adequate antidepressant trials) was appropriate for the indication sought. Brindlewood's regulatory affairs team, led by Vice President Dr. Lucinda Ferreira-Castillo, is targeting an NDA submission in Q3 2027.

ORENDEL MINING CORPORATION
Operations Report — Third Quarter 2023
Hovdalen Mine Complex, Telemark County, Norway

Project Overview

The Hovdalen Mine Complex is a polymetallic underground operation located 34 kilometers northeast of Notodden in Telemark County, Norway. Orendel Mining Corporation, incorporated in Toronto, Ontario, holds a 78% operating interest in the project through its wholly-owned Norwegian subsidiary, Orendel Norden AS. The remaining 22% is held by Statens Mineralselskap, a Norwegian state entity. Hovdalen was commissioned in October 2009 following a $680 million development capital program and has been in continuous production since. The mine extracts copper-gold ore from the Hovdalen Skarn deposit, with secondary by-product credits from zinc and silver.

Mineral Reserves

As of December 31, 2022, total proven and probable mineral reserves at Hovdalen are estimated at 847 million metric tonnes grading 0.41% copper equivalent, 0.19 grams per tonne gold, and 0.33% zinc. The reserve estimate was prepared by independent Qualified Person Dr. Ragnhild Thoresen of Behling Mineral Services in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 standards. At current production rates, the reserve supports a remaining mine life of approximately 24 years.

Q3 2023 Production Results

Ore extraction in Q3 2023 totaled 11.7 million metric tonnes, a 4.2% increase from Q3 2022's 11.23 million tonnes. Copper production for the quarter was 41,800 metric tonnes (payable), below the Q3 guidance range of 43,000–45,000 metric tonnes due to lower-than-expected mill recoveries of 84.3% against a planned 87.0%. The recovery shortfall was attributed to elevated silicate gangue content in the eastern sublevel stopes accessed during September. Gold by-product production totaled 18,740 troy ounces, generating $35.7 million in by-product credits at an average realized price of $1,903 per troy ounce.

Cash costs per pound of copper produced, net of by-product credits, were $1.87/lb in Q3 2023, compared to $1.64/lb in Q3 2022. The year-over-year cost increase reflects a 14.7% rise in Norwegian labor costs following the June 2023 national wage settlement, higher energy input costs (electricity purchases totaled $22.4 million in Q3, up from $18.9 million in Q3 2022), and $3.1 million in additional ground support materials installed following a pore pressure alert in the T-14 stoping block on September 4.

Safety Performance

The Hovdalen Complex recorded a Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (RIFR) of 0.52 per 200,000 hours worked for the twelve months ending September 30, 2023, compared to 0.71 for the same period ending September 30, 2022. There were no lost-time injuries during Q3 2023. The September 4 pore pressure event required evacuation of 47 workers from affected areas for a period of 6 hours; no injuries occurred and monitoring over the subsequent three weeks indicated stabilization of the affected zone. Orendel retained Bergmekanikk AS of Trondheim to conduct an independent geotechnical review, with a report expected by December 15, 2023.

Capital Expenditure

Capital expenditures in Q3 2023 totaled $47.3 million, comprising $29.1 million of sustaining capital (principally underground development, ventilation upgrades, and mobile equipment rebuilds) and $18.2 million of growth capital related to the Level 12 expansion program. The Level 12 program targets access to higher-grade copper zones in the central deposit at depths between 1,400 and 1,650 meters below surface. Total approved budget for Level 12 is $214 million, with $87.4 million spent through September 30.

Financial Performance

Q3 2023 revenue was $201.4 million, comprising $165.7 million from copper sales, $35.7 million in gold by-product credits, and minor zinc and silver revenues. EBITDA for the quarter was $94.7 million, representing a margin of 47.0%. Net income attributable to Orendel shareholders (78% interest) was $38.6 million. The company's capital allocation policy targets a quarterly dividend of CAD $0.14 per share, unchanged since Q1 2021.

BRIGHTWATER MUNICIPAL WATER AUTHORITY
Annual Operations and Capital Report — Fiscal Year 2023

Authority Overview

The Brightwater Municipal Water Authority was established by joint resolution of the Caldwell County Board of Supervisors and the Millford City Council on March 14, 1974 to provide centralized water and wastewater services to the greater Millford metropolitan area. The Authority's service territory encompasses a resident population of 214,000 within Millford city limits and an additional 87,400 residents in unincorporated Caldwell County served under an intergovernmental agreement renewed most recently on July 1, 2020 for a term of 20 years.

The Authority operates three water treatment plants. The Eastside Water Treatment Plant has a permitted capacity of 48 million gallons per day (MGD) and underwent its most recent major rehabilitation in 2017 at a cost of $34.1 million. The Westbrook Water Treatment Plant has a permitted capacity of 22 MGD and serves the western portions of the service territory. The Millford Heights Satellite Plant, completed in 2019 at a cost of $8.7 million, has a capacity of 6 MGD and operates seasonally from May through September to meet peak demand.

Fiscal Year 2023 Operations

Total potable water produced during FY2023 (July 1, 2022 – June 30, 2023) was 19.84 billion gallons, a 1.7% decrease from FY2022's 20.18 billion gallons attributable to milder summer temperatures and increased implementation of tiered pricing for irrigation accounts. Average daily production was 54.4 million gallons per day, peaking at 71.2 MGD on July 18, 2022, the highest single-day demand in Authority history.

The Authority's distribution network consists of 1,847 miles of water main ranging in diameter from 4 inches to 48 inches. During FY2023, the Authority responded to 741 water main breaks, a 12.3% decrease from FY2022's 834 breaks. The average restoration time per break event was 4.7 hours. The Authority's annual main replacement program targeted 18.4 miles of aged cast-iron main, replacing an average of 1.0% of the legacy cast-iron inventory per year.

Water Quality

The Authority's Eastside and Westbrook plants both achieved compliance with all primary drinking water standards throughout FY2023. The UV disinfection upgrade at Eastside, completed October 1, 2022 at a cost of $6.4 million, brought UV compliance from 94.2% to 99.8% of sampled hours meeting the 40 mJ/cm² inactivation standard for Cryptosporidium. Quarterly monitoring detected no measurable lead concentrations above 5 parts per billion in the 97th-percentile sample set drawn from 240 representative service lines across the system.

Non-Revenue Water

System-wide water loss for FY2023 was 11.3% of total production, representing approximately 2.24 billion gallons. This figure includes real losses (leakage from mains, service connections, and storage facilities) and apparent losses (meter inaccuracies and unauthorized use). The Authority's water loss control program, operated in partnership with Utility Technical Services Inc. of Columbus, Ohio, deployed acoustic leak detection on 847 miles of main during FY2023. The Authority's target is to reduce non-revenue water to below 9.0% by FY2027.

Financial Summary

Total operating revenues in FY2023 were $94.7 million, comprising $78.3 million in water service charges, $11.4 million in wastewater services billed under a joint operations agreement with Caldwell County Sanitation District, and $5.0 million in connection fees and miscellaneous revenues. Operating expenses totaled $71.2 million, yielding net operating income of $23.5 million and a debt service coverage ratio of 1.47, above the 1.25 minimum required under the Authority's outstanding bond indentures.

Total long-term debt outstanding as of June 30, 2023 was $187 million, including $143 million in Series 2018 revenue bonds bearing a coupon of 3.84% maturing in 2043, and $44 million in State Revolving Fund loans at a blended rate of 1.9%.

Capital Program

The Authority's approved FY2024–FY2028 Capital Improvement Plan totals $214.7 million, with the largest single project being the Eastside Plant Membrane Filtration Upgrade at $67.3 million, scheduled for design in FY2024 and construction in FY2025–FY2027. On November 14, 2023, the Authority Board approved a contract with Cyberworks Infrastructure LLC for SCADA system replacement at all three treatment plants and 14 remote pump stations for a total of $3.2 million, with implementation targeted for completion by June 30, 2025.

KESTREL FINANCIAL PARTNERS
Annual Investor Letter — Fiscal Year 2023

Firm Background

Kestrel Financial Partners was founded in 2012 by Managing Partners Elliot Granzow and Sondra Bathurst-Nkrumah to pursue control-oriented private equity investments in lower middle market industrial and business services companies in the United States. Kestrel's investment thesis focuses on companies with revenues between $30 million and $120 million that exhibit defensible market positions, recurring revenue characteristics, and meaningful operational improvement opportunities. The firm is headquartered at 1170 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2400, Atlanta, Georgia.

Fund I Performance Update

Kestrel Partners Fund I, LP closed in September 2013 at $342 million in total committed capital from 23 limited partners, including seven public pension funds, four university endowments, two insurance general accounts, and ten family offices. The fund made 11 platform investments and 14 add-on acquisitions during its investment period, which concluded in September 2017. As of December 31, 2023, Fund I has returned $687 million in distributions to limited partners against $342 million in contributed capital, representing a 2.01x distributed multiple on invested capital.

The fund's most significant realized investment was Cascade Thermal Solutions, an HVAC services business serving commercial customers in the Pacific Northwest acquired in November 2014 for $38.7 million (entry multiple of 6.2x EBITDA). Under Kestrel's ownership, Cascade completed four bolt-on acquisitions totaling $14.3 million and expanded from 3 branch locations to 11. The company was sold in March 2019 to Meridian Services Group for $87 million, representing a gross return of $52.3 million and a 3.4x gross money-on-invested-capital multiple. The gross IRR on Cascade was 28.7%.

The fund's largest unrealized position is Pinnacle Workforce Solutions, a temporary staffing and permanent placement firm serving light industrial and logistics clients in the upper Midwest, acquired in August 2018 for $61.4 million at 7.8x trailing EBITDA. As of December 31, 2023, Pinnacle has achieved cumulative EBITDA growth of 47% from the acquisition date and the Fund I carrying value reflects a mark of 2.1x invested capital based on a current enterprise value assessment of $128.9 million.

Fund I Net Asset Value and Remaining Portfolio

Fund I net asset value as of December 31, 2023 is $94.3 million across three remaining active holdings, reflecting audited fair values prepared by the portfolio company accounting teams and reviewed by the independent valuation firm Stonebridge Valuation Advisors of Charlotte, North Carolina. The blended gross IRR across all realized and unrealized Fund I investments is 21.8% as of December 31, 2023.

Fund II Overview

Kestrel Partners Fund II, LP held its final close on March 7, 2022 at $487 million in total committed capital from 31 limited partners. Fund II's management fee is 1.75% on committed capital during the investment period (defined as five years from final close) and 1.75% on net invested capital thereafter. The carried interest rate is 20% above an 8% preferred return with a 100% general partner catch-up provision. As of December 31, 2023, Fund II has made four platform investments with aggregate invested capital of $183.4 million and two add-on acquisitions totaling $28.7 million in consideration. The investment period will expire on March 7, 2027.

Fund II's first platform investment, Harrowgate Document Management LLC, was acquired in October 2022 for $44.7 million (7.4x EBITDA). Harrowgate provides secure document storage, digitization, and destruction services to financial services and healthcare clients in the southeastern United States. Revenue at acquisition was $31.2 million; revenue for the twelve months ending September 30, 2023 was $38.4 million, reflecting organic growth of 14.1% and the addition of one tuck-in acquisition closed in April 2023 for $8.2 million.

NORDHOLM AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVE
Annual Report to Members — Fiscal Year 2023
(Year Ended August 31, 2023)

Cooperative History and Structure

Nordholm Agricultural Cooperative was organized under the Minnesota Agricultural Cooperative Act in February 1947 by 84 founding member-farmers in Clearwater and Polk Counties. The cooperative's primary business lines are grain merchandising, agronomy inputs, energy distribution, and crop insurance services. Current membership stands at 1,847 active farm operations, representing approximately 2.1 million acres of enrolled land, primarily in corn, soybeans, sunflowers, and spring wheat. Nordholm's administrative headquarters is located in Crookston, Minnesota. The cooperative employs 487 full-time and 213 seasonal employees.

Grain Operations

Nordholm operates 14 grain elevators with a combined licensed storage capacity of 63.4 million bushels, distributed across Clearwater, Polk, Red Lake, and Pennington Counties. During FY2023, total grain receipts at Nordholm facilities were 187.4 million bushels, a 4.8% increase from FY2022's 178.8 million bushels. The Grafton elevator location handled 21.4 million bushels, making it the cooperative's highest-volume facility. Corn accounted for 47.3% of total receipts (88.6 million bushels), soybeans for 31.4% (58.8 million bushels), and wheat and other small grains for the remaining 21.3%.

In July 2022, the cooperative's Grafton elevator sustained significant structural damage from a grain dust explosion that occurred during a dust collection system maintenance procedure. The incident resulted in the total loss of the 2.4-million-bushel concrete elevator annex constructed in 1968. Property damage was estimated at $2.4 million by the cooperative's insurer, Heartland Mutual Insurance, which settled the claim in full in October 2022. The Grafton facility returned to full operational capacity by March 1, 2023 following reconstruction.

Agronomy Services

Nordholm's agronomy division recorded sales of fertilizer, seed, and crop protection products totaling $341.7 million in FY2023, a decrease of 8.3% from FY2022's $372.8 million, reflecting lower nitrogen fertilizer prices compared to the prior year's historically elevated levels. The division applied precision variable-rate fertilizer prescriptions on 487,000 acres under management agreements, up from 341,000 acres in FY2022. The agronomy division contributed $14.8 million in operating margin to the cooperative's consolidated results.

Financial Results

Consolidated net savings (equivalent to net income under cooperative accounting) for FY2023 were $38.4 million, compared to $41.2 million in FY2022. The decrease reflects lower agronomy margins partially offset by improved grain merchandising results. Total assets as of August 31, 2023 were $487.3 million. Long-term debt outstanding was $87.3 million, consisting of a $62.0 million term loan facility with AgriBank FCB maturing in 2031 (fixed rate 4.12%) and $25.3 million in equipment notes. The cooperative's equity-to-assets ratio was 42.7%, up from 40.1% in FY2022.

Patronage allocations for FY2023 totaled $28.7 million, of which 60% ($17.2 million) was distributed as cash patronage dividends to members in November 2023, with the remaining 40% ($11.5 million) retained as allocated equity.

Capital Investment Program

The Board of Directors approved a capital investment program of $22.1 million for FY2024, comprising $9.4 million for elevator aeration and handling equipment upgrades across six locations, $7.8 million for the construction of a new 1.8-million-bushel flat storage facility at the Mentor, Minnesota location, and $4.9 million for agronomy facility improvements including a new liquid fertilizer storage tank at the Crookston plant with a capacity of 400,000 gallons.

HARBRIDGE RESEARCH INSTITUTE
Annual Research Report — Fiscal Year 2023

Institute Overview

The Harbridge Research Institute is an independent, not-for-profit applied research organization founded in 1961 and headquartered in Hanover, New Hampshire. The Institute conducts sponsored and internally funded research in advanced materials science, structural engineering, and protective coatings, with a primary emphasis on applications for extreme operating environments. The Institute maintains laboratory facilities at Hanover and at a satellite campus in Albany, New York established in 2004. Total research staff as of June 30, 2023 comprises 147 full-time researchers, 34 postdoctoral associates, and 89 graduate student researchers enrolled through degree programs at Dartmouth College and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

External Funding

External sponsored research revenues for FY2023 (October 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023) totaled $34.7 million, a 12.0% increase from FY2022's $31.0 million. The Office of Naval Research (ONR) remains the Institute's largest sponsor, providing $14.3 million under a five-year Multidisciplinary Research Program of the University Navy (MURI) award focused on high-entropy alloy fatigue behavior. The Department of Energy contributed $9.4 million through three separate grants in the areas of thermal barrier coatings, corrosion monitoring, and hydrogen embrittlement detection. DARPA provided $4.8 million for classified materials characterization work under Program Manager Dr. Seth Villanueva. Commercial contracts with industrial partners accounted for the remaining $6.2 million in external revenue.

Endowment and Finances

The Institute's endowment stands at $78.4 million as of September 30, 2023, invested under a diversified policy allocation of 55% global equities, 25% fixed income, 15% alternative investments, and 5% cash equivalents. The endowment returned 9.4% on a total return basis for FY2023. Annual payout from the endowment to support operations was $3.1 million, representing a 4.0% spending rate. Total operating expenditures in FY2023 were $47.3 million against revenues of $47.8 million, producing a modest operating surplus of $0.5 million. The FY2024 budget approved by the Board of Directors on November 9, 2023 increases total operating expenditures to $41.2 million — a projection that assumes $38.9 million in external revenue based on anticipated new awards.

High-Entropy Alloy Research Program

The Institute's flagship research program involves synthesis and characterization of novel high-entropy alloys (HEAs) for structural applications at temperatures above 900°C. During FY2023, the research team led by Dr. Yusuf Adegboyega identified a five-component alloy system designated HIA-7741 (nominally equimolar Cr-Mo-Nb-Ta-W) that demonstrated exceptional combined strength and toughness. In standardized testing under ASTM E8/E8M, HIA-7741 exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of 1,247 megapascals and a 0.2% offset yield strength of 1,081 megapascals at 25°C. Fracture toughness (KIc) measured by single-edge notched bend specimens per ASTM E1820 was 83 MPa·m^0.5, substantially above the 47 MPa·m^0.5 average of legacy nickel superalloys tested in the same campaign. A provisional patent application (Serial No. 63/441,287) was filed on August 3, 2023.

Protective Coatings Program

The Institute's coatings group, led by Dr. Amara Osei-Mensah, evaluated twelve candidate thermal barrier coating systems under cyclic oxidation conditions simulating gas turbine operating environments (1,100°C peak, 100-cycle test protocol per GE Aviation specification GE-S1000-1). System D, a novel yttria-stabilized zirconia formulation incorporating 3.2 mol% hafnium oxide as a stabilizer, achieved 94.3% retained coating integrity after 100 cycles, compared to 78.7% for the current best-in-class commercial system designated System A (a standard 7 wt% YSZ deposited by air plasma spray). Four of the twelve systems tested showed integrity below 60% after 100 cycles and were eliminated from further consideration.

FY2024 Research Priorities

The Board of Directors identified three priority research areas for FY2024 investment: (1) scale-up of HIA-7741 synthesis to 50-kilogram heats using vacuum arc remelting at the Albany facility, targeting characterization of mechanical properties at elevated temperatures (600°C and 900°C test campaigns); (2) a new program in additive manufacturing of refractory HEA components, for which the Institute has submitted a $7.4 million proposal to ONR; and (3) expansion of the coatings program to include environmental barrier coatings for silicon carbide ceramic matrix composites, in partnership with Ceramics Research Consortium member General Dynamics Mission Systems.
